title: Remission is not bare penalty-relaxation while we stay unrenewed
source_text: VII. Sed Christus non simpliciter morte sua nos praestat a peccato immunes. Neque putandum est Deum, quum nobis peccata propter Christum remittit, solummodo poenam peccati relaxare, dum peccatores interim, sicut antea, in nobis remanemus: quemadmodum Principes terreni dicuntur facinoroso crimina remittere, quum illum justo alioquin supplicio eximunt, etiamsi per id nihil interius immutetur, sed maneat talis qualis antea erat.
pass_a_gloss: But Christ does not by his death simply render us immune from sin. Nor is it to be thought that God, when he remits our sins for Christ's sake, only relaxes the penalty of sin, while meanwhile we remain sinners in ourselves as before: just as earthly princes are said to remit crimes to a criminal when they exempt him from an otherwise just punishment, even if by that nothing is changed inwardly, but he remains such as he was before.
pass_b_english: Cross-remission is not a prince's bare stay of punishment while the sinner stays inwardly unchanged.
